The question now is what safeguards Google puts in place before Gemini operates at wider scale.

Iran War Cost US $38 Billion, Drained Missile Stockpile

2026-W38 7 outlets SRQ
0.84 V2×17 V3×1

The Congressional Budget Office found the US war in Iran has cost at least $38 billion and that the depleted US missile stockpile may take 5 years to fully rebuild.

Full Narration

The US war in Iran has cost at least $38 billion. That figure comes from the Congressional Budget Office, which released its assessment this week. Pentagon auditors put the figure slightly lower, at $33 billion. The CBO report also found that the US missile stockpile could take 5 years to rebuild. That's the more consequential long-term finding — weapons expended in the conflict can't be replaced quickly, regardless of when the fighting ends. The financial cost puts the Iran conflict among the most expensive US military actions in recent history. The 5-year replenishment timeline is what defense planners will be focused on as the administration considers its next moves in the region.

The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points, marking the first rate increase in 3 years and signaling a shift in monetary policy.

Full Narration

For the first time in 3 years, the Federal Reserve has raised interest rates. The Fed increased its benchmark rate by 25 basis points this week, reversing a prolonged hold that followed years of cuts. The hike signals the Fed sees inflation pressures that require tightening. For borrowers, that means higher costs on mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards, effective immediately. Pay attention to whether the Fed signals additional increases are coming — that's the figure that will move markets in the weeks ahead.

EPA Overturns Biden Power Plant Pollution Limits

2026-W38 9 outlets SRQ
0.56 V1×6 V2×4 V4×2 V5×2

The Trump EPA overturned a Biden-era rule capping greenhouse gas emissions from power plants, stating that such emissions have no material impact on climate change.

Full Narration

The Trump administration has overturned the Biden-era rule limiting greenhouse gas emissions from power plants. The EPA's rollback removes pollution caps that had required plants to adopt carbon controls or phase down output. The EPA stated that power plant emissions have no material impact on climate change — a position that directly contradicts the scientific consensus underpinning the original rule. The Biden rule had targeted the electricity sector as a primary driver of US emissions. The rollback is expected to face legal challenges. The signal to watch is whether federal courts apply the Supreme Court's 2022 West Virginia v. EPA ruling, which restricted how broadly the agency can regulate power sector emissions, as a barrier to any future reinstatement.

Earth lost 12 trillion tons of ice in 47 years

3 articles tracked Relevance: 0.31 Verification threshold ✓

Satellite data reveals that Earth lost over 12 trillion tons of ice from Greenland and Antarctica between 1976 and 2023, primarily due to warming temperatures from climate change. This massive ice loss contributes to rising sea levels, threatening coastal communities and ecosystems worldwide while accelerating the pace of climate change.
